skill.name: ripgrep
skill.description: Use when searching code fast with ripgrep (rg): recursive regex search that respects .gitignore, with type filters, case control, and globs.
whenToUse: Searching a large codebase for a string or regex quickly
Filtering matches by file type or glob pattern
Listing files that contain (or omit) a pattern
Replacing slow grep -r pipelines in scripts and editors

keyConcepts.explanation: rg skips files matched by .gitignore, .ignore, and hidden files by default, which is why results differ from grep -r.
`--type` / `-t` restricts search to a language (e.g. py, js); `rg --type-list` shows all defined types.
Pass `-S` for smart case: case-insensitive when the pattern is all lowercase, case-sensitive otherwise; `-i` forces insensitive.
`-g` includes/excludes paths by glob, e.g. `-g '*.rs'` or `-g '!test/**'` to negate.
rg uses Rust's linear-time regex (no backreferences); pass `-P` for the PCRE2 engine when you need lookaround or backrefs.
`-F` treats the pattern literally so regex metacharacters are matched as-is.

apiReference.purpose: Recursively search for a regex pattern from PATH (default cwd).
Limit search to files of a given type.
List matching files (-l), count per file (-c), glob filter (-g), whole-word (-w).

gotchas: rg ignores files listed in .gitignore and hidden files by default; use -u, -uu, or -uuu to relax (the last also searches binary files).
The default regex engine rejects backreferences and lookaround; use -P for PCRE2 if it was compiled in.
Patterns starting with - are parsed as flags; use -e PATTERN or put -- before the pattern.
rg searches recursively by default, so `rg foo` with no path covers the whole tree, unlike grep.
-t/--type needs a known type name; for ad-hoc extensions use -g '*.ext' instead.
Output is colorized and grouped for TTYs but flat when piped, which can surprise scripts parsing output.
